title: DR1 saves — or refuses to leave — a part-filled add-a-document form when the trader presses Save and continue; the frontend throws the answers away without a word.

finding.frontend: Continue never looks at the add-a-document form. The post handler branches on the action: 'add' validates and saves, a remove action removes, and everything else falls through to a check on whether any already-saved document is still being scanned and then a redirect to the next page (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/controller.js:255-279). A trader who types a reference, picks a date, chooses a file and then presses Continue instead of "Save and add another" loses all three silently — no error, no saved record, and no warning that the page they are leaving is now empty. No captured frontend state shows this; it is read from the handler.
finding.prototype: DR1 treats Save and continue as a save. Uploads stay optional, but once a document type has been chosen the whole add form is validated before the trader can leave, and if it passes the document is added on the way out (app/routes.js:10174-10193, whose own comment states the rule as "uploads are optional, but once a document type is chosen all document fields must be completed before continuing"). dr1-upload-documents-continue-error captures the refusal: three errors — "Enter a document reference", "Enter a date of issue", "Upload a document" — on a form where only the document type had been filled in and no document had been saved.
finding.difference: On Continue, look at the add-a-document form before redirecting. If any of its fields carries an answer, run the same validation the Add action runs and either save the document or re-render with the errors; if every field is empty, continue as now. DR1 uses the document type as the trigger for this, and the frontend has no such field today, so the trigger has to be "any field answered" until the type select lands. Scope this to Continue only: the two exit actions beside it discard the part-filled form as well, but so does DR1's own "Save and return to overview", so changing them would move the frontend away from DR1 rather than towards it.
finding.falsifiedBy: Filling the frontend's add-a-document form, pressing Continue, and finding either the document saved or an error shown.
finding.verification: Re-ran the structural claim from scratch rather than reading it. Read the frontend post handler whole at controller.js:255-279: it branches to postRemove on a retry-remove payload, to postAdd on action 'add', to postRemove on a remove action, and then falls through to `loadPage` plus `if (!kit.hubExitTarget(request) && isStillSettling(pageState.documents))` before redirecting to `kit.nextTarget`. There is no read of accompanyingDocumentReference, accompanyingDocumentDateOfIssue or the file part on that path, so a part-filled form is discarded with no error and no record — the claim is exact. The author's disproof of the pairing note also holds: cannotContinue reaches the page only through settlingSummaryErrors (scan/summary-errors.js:21-24), which is keyed on scanStatus, never on the add form. On the DR1 side, routes.js:10173-10193 gates validateUploadDocument on `getDocumentTypeValues(...).includes(values.documentType)` and calls addUploadedDocument on the way out, and dr1-upload-documents-continue-error shows the select holding `itahc` with the three errors and no saved-documents table in the DOM. CORRECT on the claim; two repairs made, see correction.
finding.correction: Two repairs, neither touching the central claim. First, `controls` named only "Save and continue", which exists on dr1-upload-documents-continue-error and on neither frontend screen — the frontend's primary button reads "Continue" — so the crop would have failed on fe-documents-empty and fe-documents-populated and fallen back to a whole-page shot. "Continue" added ahead of it. Second, the difference slot closed with "The same rule applies to the two exit actions beside Continue, which take the trader off the page just as finally." That asks the frontend to do something DR1 does not do: DR1's soft-save exit calls resetUploadDocumentFormState and redirects without validating or saving (routes.js:10167-10171), discarding the form exactly as the frontend does. The sentence has been replaced with the observation that the exit actions match DR1 already and are out of scope.

relatedTo.why: DR1 triggers this validation off the document type the frontend does not yet ask for
